newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia state workers to fix strike date Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: Colombia state workers to fix strike date Jan 20.

text.p: The head of Colombia's main public sector workers' union said Friday members would meet Jan. 20 to fix the start date of an indefinite, nationwide strike in protest of below-inflation rate wage rises.

Wilson Borja Diaz, chairman of the 800,000-strong FENALTRASE union, said he "rejected the government wage imposition" which granted a weighted 13.5 percent rise to state employees, announced earlier in the day -- well below 1996 inflation figures of 21.63 percent and below the 1997 target of 18 percent.
Borja Diaz said education workers, represented by the FECODE union, had agreed to join them in the strike call, which he said could take effect in "about mid-February".

Education workers will receive a rise 8 percent above other state workers as part of a 1995 deal with the government aimed at cutting their wage differential compared to other parts of the public sector.
The weighted public sector pay rise will, in practice, range between 21 percent for the lowest paid state employees to an 8 percent hike for the highest paid.

Private sector workers are also grumbling about the rise in the minimum wage, announced in late December, of 21.02 percent. Borja said he would try to convince the private sector labor federations to join the call for an indefinite nationwide strike.
